body.en: Foreign (international) trade is the exchange of goods and services between countries. It is of three types: export trade (selling goods to other countries), import trade (buying goods from other countries) and entrepot trade (importing goods in order to re-export them, often after some processing). *Foreign trade* is more complex than internal trade because of distance, different currencies, customs duties, different laws and languages, and the risks of transport and payment.

title.en: Balance of trade and balance of payments

body.en: The *balance of trade* compares the value of a country's exports and imports of goods only: a surplus when exports exceed imports, a deficit when imports exceed exports. The balance of payments is a wider record of all economic transactions with the rest of the world: goods, services, income, transfers (such as money sent home by workers abroad) and capital flows. A country can have a trade deficit but still balance its payments through earnings from services or inflows of investment.

points.en: Services and remittances can offset a *trade* deficit

problem.en: A country's exports of goods are ₹35,000 crore and imports ₹48,000 crore. Its net earnings from services and remittances are ₹15,000 crore. Comment on its balance of trade and its position overall.

steps.en: Balance of trade = 35,000 − 48,000 = −₹13,000 crore: a deficit.
Services and remittances bring in a net ₹15,000 crore.
So on these items the current position is +₹2,000 crore.
A trade deficit can be offset by invisibles such as services and remittances.

answer.en: Trade deficit of ₹13,000 crore, offset by ₹15,000 crore of invisibles.

say.en: A country's exports of goods are 35,000 rupees crore and imports 48,000 rupees crore. Its net earnings from services and remittances are 15,000 rupees crore. Comment on its balance of trade and its position overall.
Balance of trade equals 35,000 minus 48,000 equals minus 13,000 rupees crore: a deficit.
Services and remittances bring in a net 15,000 rupees crore.
So on these items the current position is plus 2,000 rupees crore.
A trade deficit can be offset by invisibles such as services and remittances.
So the answer is Trade deficit of 13,000 rupees crore, offset by 15,000 rupees crore of invisibles.
